review.method: Manual lexical and constituent correspondence against the exact pinned N1904 whitespace tokens and displayed LSV text; English supplied words and witness differences remain explicit. Inflected forms, repetition, and grammatical relations were reviewed rather than inferred from shared Strong numbers.
review.sourceTokenization: Zero-based whitespace tokens including attached punctuation.
review.limitations: This is a reviewed lexical alignment, not a claim that LSV and N1904 share every underlying reading or grammatical rendering.

4:1.sourceText: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ἐπιπόθητοι, χαρὰ καὶ στέφανός μου, οὕτως στήκετε ἐν Κυρίῳ, ἀγαπητοί.
4:1.targetText: So then, my brothers, beloved and longed for, my joy and garland, so stand in the LORD, beloved.

4:2.sourceText: Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν Κυρίῳ.
4:2.targetText: I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, to be of the same mind in the LORD;

groups.note: Actual auto is the accusative neuter singular same-pronoun, distinct from the preceding article.
Actual phronein is a present active infinitive, rendered to be of ... mind. No separate Greek being verb or mind noun is printed here.

4:3.sourceText: ναὶ ἐρωτῶ καὶ σέ, γνήσιε σύνζυγε, συνλαμβάνου αὐταῖς, αἵτινες ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ συνήθλησάν μοι μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου, ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς.
4:3.targetText: and I also ask you, genuine yoke-fellow, be assisting those women who strove along with me in the good news, with Clement also, and the others, my fellow-workers, whose names [are] in [the] Scroll of Life.

groups.note: Actual source marks this vocative singular word as an adjective in both analyses; English uses the personal designation yoke-fellow. Its source lemma remains syzygos.
Actual autais is a dative feminine plural personal pronoun. English explicitly names its referents as those women; no separate Greek woman noun or demonstrative is printed at this occurrence.

unmappedSource.reason: The affirmative particle ναί (yes/indeed) is absent from LSV. The pinned CrossWire TR witness instead has καί in position 1, accounting for the English conjunction; this is a source-witness difference.
Greek article with names is not separately rendered in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness variant: LSV begins with and, matching the pinned CrossWire TR καί; N1904 begins with the affirmative ναί. Do not pair these unlike Greek words.
Bracketed English copula supplied for a Greek verbless clause; no finite Greek copula token.
Bracketed English article supplied before Scroll; N1904 βίβλῳ has no article.

4:4.sourceText: Χαίρετε ἐν Κυρίῳ πάντοτε· πάλιν ἐρῶ, χαίρετε.
4:4.targetText: Rejoice in the LORD always; again I will say, rejoice!

4:5.sourceText: τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν γνωσθήτω πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις. ὁ Κύριος ἐγγύς·
4:5.targetText: Let your reasonableness be known to all men; the LORD [is] near;

groups.note: Actual article plus neuter singular adjective is the substantival expression rendered reasonableness. The adjective head and its article both remain; no separate Greek reasonableness noun is printed.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied for a Greek verbless clause; no finite Greek copula token.

review.note: τὸ ἐπιεικές is a substantivized adjective: reasonableness. The passive imperative γνωσθήτω supplies Let … be known; it is discontinuous around the subject.

4:6.sourceText: μηδὲν μεριμνᾶτε, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ δεήσει μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τὰ αἰτήματα ὑμῶν γνωριζέσθω πρὸς τὸν Θεόν.
4:6.targetText: be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer, and by supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.
Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:8.sourceText: Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί, ὅσα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ὅσα σεμνά, ὅσα δίκαια, ὅσα ἁγνά, ὅσα προσφιλῆ, ὅσα εὔφημα, εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος, ταῦτα λογίζεσθε·
4:8.targetText: As to the rest, brothers, as many things as are true, as many as [are] revered, as many as [are] righteous, as many as [are] pure, as many as [are] lovely, as many as [are] of good report, if any worthiness, and if any praise, think on these things;

4:9.sourceText: ἃ καὶ ἐμάθετε καὶ παρελάβετε καὶ ἠκούσατε καὶ εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοί, ταῦτα πράσσετε· καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
4:9.targetText: the things that you also learned, and receive, and hear, and saw in me, do those, and the God of peace will be with you.

groups.note: Actual parelabete is a second-aorist active indicative, second person plural, in both source analyses and the printed TR. LSV prints receive; the original is not retagged as present.
Actual ekousate is an aorist active indicative, second person plural, in both source analyses and the printed TR. LSV prints hear; the actual past-form occurrence remains.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article with peace is omitted in the English phrase of peace.

review.note: LSV receive and hear are retained exactly as displayed, although παρελάβετε and ἠκούσατε are aorist indicative. The links express lexical correspondence, not English tense equivalence.

4:10.sourceText: Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ μεγάλως ὅτι ἤδη ποτὲ ἀνεθάλετε τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν· ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε, ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ.
4:10.targetText: And I rejoiced in the LORD greatly, that now at length you flourished again in caring for me, for which also you were caring, and lacked opportunity;

groups.note: Actual article and present active infinitive phronein form the caring expression. The later imperfect finite ephroneite retains its separate occurrence; no caring noun is fabricated.
Actual ekaireisthe is an imperfect nonactive verb of lacking an opportunity, rendered lacked opportunity. The source has no separate opportunity noun at this occurrence.

review.note: τὸ … φρονεῖν is the nominalized infinitive rendered in caring. Its tokens are discontinuous around ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ (for me).

4:11.sourceText: οὐχ ὅτι καθ’ ὑστέρησιν λέγω· ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον ἐν οἷς εἰμι αὐτάρκης εἶναι.
4:11.targetText: I do not say that in respect of want, for I learned in the things in which I am—to be content;

4:12.sourceText: οἶδα καὶ ταπεινοῦσθαι, οἶδα καὶ περισσεύειν· ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν μεμύημαι, καὶ χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾶν, καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι.
4:12.targetText: I have known both to be abased, and I have known to abound; in everything and in all things I have been initiated, both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in want.

review.note: Retains the prior explicitly reviewed mapping. μεμύημαι is I have been initiated, χορτάζεσθαι is to be full, and παντί/πᾶσιν are everything/all things. Raw LSV USFM Strong tags are not used.

4:13.sourceText: πάντα ἰσχύω ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί με.
4:13.targetText: I have strength for all things, in Christ’s strengthening me;

groups.note: Actual ischyo is a present active first-person singular verb, rendered I have strength for. There is no separate Greek strength noun here.

unmappedSource.reason: Article substantivizes the participle: the one strengthening. LSV replaces this with a possessive proper name, so no independent English article/relative is present.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV names Christ; the complete printed TR appends Christo, but N1904 has no Christos word here. The actual article and strengthening participle do not supply a printed proper name.

review.note: The shared participle is strengthening. Christ’s is explicitly unpaired because N1904 reads ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί με without Χριστός; this does not imply an exact shared witness.

4:14.sourceText: πλὴν καλῶς ἐποιήσατε συνκοινωνήσαντές μου τῇ θλίψει.
4:14.targetText: but you did well, having shared in my tribulation;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:15.sourceText: οἴδατε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς, Φιλιππήσιοι, ὅτι ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ὅτε ἐξῆλθον ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας, οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι,
4:15.targetText: and you have known, even you Philippians, that in the beginning of the good news when I went forth from Macedonia, no assembly communicated with me in regard to giving and receiving except you only;

groups.note: Actual eis plus accusative logos is the account/matter construction rendered in regard to. Logos is the noun head; no peri preposition or different Greek regard word is substituted.
Actual doseos is a genitive singular noun of giving, rendered giving. It is not a separately printed didomi verb.
Actual lempseos is a genitive singular receiving noun, rendered receiving. It is not a separately printed lambano verb.

4:16.sourceText: ὅτι καὶ ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δὶς εἰς τὴν χρείαν μοι ἐπέμψατε.
4:16.targetText: because in Thessalonica also, both once and again you sent to my need;

groups.note: Actual dis is the adverb used in the attested once-and-again expression; it is not a printed palin occurrence.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:17.sourceText: οὐχ ὅτι ἐπιζητῶ τὸ δόμα, ἀλλὰ ἐπιζητῶ τὸν καρπὸν τὸν πλεονάζοντα εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν.
4:17.targetText: not that I seek after the gift, but I seek after the fruit that is overflowing to your account;

4:18.sourceText: ἀπέχω δὲ πάντα καὶ περισσεύω· πεπλήρωμαι δεξάμενος παρὰ Ἐπαφροδίτου τὰ παρ’ ὑμῶν, ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, θυσίαν δεκτήν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ.
4:18.targetText: and I have all things, and abound; I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you—an odor of a refreshing fragrance—a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God:

groups.note: Actual ta is the accusative neuter plural article before the from-you phrase, used substantivally as the things. No independent Greek thing noun is printed.
Actual euodias is a genitive singular fragrance noun expanded as of a refreshing fragrance. The source does not contain a separate refreshing adjective.

4:19.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεός μου πληρώσει πᾶσαν χρείαν ὑμῶν κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτοῦ ἐν δόξῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
4:19.targetText: and my God will supply all your need, according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.
Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:20.sourceText: τῷ δὲ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ ἡμῶν ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
4:20.targetText: and to God, even our Father, [is] the glory through the ages of the ages. Amen.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied for a Greek verbless clause; no finite Greek copula token.

4:21.sourceText: Ἀσπάσασθε πάντα ἅγιον ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ. ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ ἀδελφοί.
4:21.targetText: Every holy one in Christ Jesus greets you; the brothers with me greet you;

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 Aspasasthe is a second-person plural imperative in both source analyses; the complete printed TR likewise has the imperative. LSV instead makes every holy one the subject of greets; this changed predicate/argument frame remains unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV changes the first printed N1904/TR imperative Greet every holy one to Every holy one greets you, introducing an object you in that clause. The distinct later plural greeting and its actual you retain their own source occurrences.

review.note: A translation-level grammatical discrepancy is retained explicitly. The shared lexical noun phrase is linked, but the first greets you is not falsely assigned to the second Greek clause or to an imperative with reversed argument roles.

4:22.sourceText: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι, μάλιστα δὲ οἱ ἐκ τῆς Καίσαρος οἰκίας.
4:22.targetText: all the holy ones greet you, and especially those of Caesar’s house.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this possessive or proper-name phrase.

4:23.sourceText: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν.
4:23.targetText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [is] with you all! Amen.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and Lord noun jointly supply of ... Lord. The intervening English our remains separately explained as a witness addition, and the actual Jesus/Christ names retain their own distinct source occurrences.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has τοῦ πνεύματος, the spirit, absent from the LSV ending with you all.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV and the printed TR have the our-reading, but pinned N1904 has no hemon word here.
Bracketed English copula supplied for a Greek verbless clause; no finite Greek copula token.
The printed TR has panton and LSV has all; pinned N1904 instead retains the spirit phrase and has no all word.
LSV and the printed TR include Amen; pinned N1904 ends with hymon and has no amen word.

review.note: N1904 with your spirit versus LSV with you all is a witness difference; only the shared plural second-person pronoun is linked. Unshared spirit/all/our/Amen are explicit.
